overview.headline: How air density speed shape and reference area set aerodynamic drag

keyPoints.point: drag depends on air density and on the square of velocity plus viscosity effects
keyPoints.quote: Drag depends on the density of the air, the square of the velocity, the air’s viscosity and compressibility

keyPoints.point: drag equals drag coefficient times density times half velocity squared times reference area
keyPoints.quote: drag D is equal to the drag coefficient Cd times the density rho (ρ) times half of the velocity V squared times the reference area A

keyPoints.point: drag coefficient includes form drag plus skin friction plus wave plus induced components
keyPoints.quote: The drag coefficient given above includes form drag, skin friction drag, wave drag, and induced drag components.

keyPoints.point: combination called dynamic pressure groups density with square of velocity divided for flow pressure
keyPoints.quote: The combination of terms “density times the square of the velocity divided by two” is called the dynamic pressure

keyTerms.gloss: variable that gathers shape and flow effects for drag calculation
keyTerms.quote: drag D is equal to the drag coefficient Cd times the density rho (ρ) times half of the velocity V squared times the reference area A

keyTerms.gloss: chosen area size used to characterize drag dependence on body size
keyTerms.quote: Notice that the area (A) given in the drag equation is given as a reference area.

keyTerms.gloss: grouping of density and velocity squared that appears in flow pressure relations
keyTerms.quote: The combination of terms “density times the square of the velocity divided by two” is called the dynamic pressure

keyTerms.gloss: density of air designated by rho in the equation
keyTerms.quote: In the equation given above, the density is designated by the letter rho (ρ).
